correctness.rationale: For n≥3 the first cosine vector has unit norm, zero sum and P_*y=cy, with c>0. For z_j=(c+cos((2j−1)π/n)/c)/n, product-to-sum gives z_j+z_{j+1}=2y_jy_{j+1} and summation gives ∑z_j=c. Row stochasticity and symmetry yield yᵀPy−c=∑P_jj(y_j²−z_j). The summands have coefficients zero at the endpoints and strictly positive in the interior because cos((2j−1)π/n)<c there. Therefore s²−c²−||(P−P_*)y||²=(s²−||Py||²)+2c(yᵀPy−c) is a sum of nonnegative terms. Equality forces all interior holding probabilities to vanish, hence the alternating family. The product with y is the negative discrete derivative of the weighted deviations with u₀=u_n=0. To prove sufficiency, test the perturbation on normalized cosine modes: each edge difference for mode r is proportional to sin(irπ/n), and multiplying by the alternating sign and taking the discrete derivative gives −2t sin(rπ/n)v_(n−r), also at the endpoints because the sine differences at i=0,n vanish. Hence the (r,n−r) block squares to [cos²(rπ/n)+4t²sin²(rπ/n)] times the identity; the unpaired even-size mode has eigenvalue −2t and the constant stays fixed. For |2t|≤1 the first pair has maximal nonconstant modulus, including |2t|=1, proving the equality, sharp coefficient and exact formula. The positive edge differences show uniqueness of P_* from the squared bound; the centered indicator on the first i sites gives the stated prefactor for edge recovery. Taylor expansion at t=0 has strictly positive quadratic coefficient, so the inverse exponent 1/2 is optimal for each fixed n. None of these steps requires an irreducible or aperiodic chain.
residual_risks: The frozen checker was inspected, not replayed. Its 4,899 floating-point trials are finite corroboration; two-vertex trials are supplementary and outside the stated n≥3 theorem.

value.rationale: The squared-deficit equality classification describes exactly which paths saturate the stability constraint, even away from the known optimum. The matching explicit perturbations and coordinate bounds quantify how far a near-optimal kernel can move on any edge and explain why the excess rate can only recover the kernel at square-root scale. This is additional information not supplied by the optimizer or by the mechanical inequality alone.
residual_risks: The coordinate prefactors are upper bounds and are not asserted optimal. The result is specific to the symmetric uniform path setting.
